::: {.callout-note title="Idea (author notes: replace before publishing)"}
A generic optimization project: fill open positions at the lowest cost. Candidate objective: overtime pay plus a weighted cost for moving people. Other factors: travel distance as a tie-breaker.

Possible two-phase approach: phase 1 reshuffles non-overtime personnel into existing gaps; phase 2 fills what remains from the overtime pool at minimal cost. Noted weakness: phase 1 can leave a more expensive overtime fill.

Constraints: headcount, role (officer, engineer, firefighter), and specialty minimums per unit. Candidate pools come from eligibility rules (for example overtime caps over past windows, overtime sign-up). Inputs: a personnel table and a unit-requirements table. Selling point: estimate the overtime hours and cost that would have been saved had the model been applied historically, using synthetic data.

Complex, enterprise or graduate-level; a model that ignores constraints isn't useful.
:::
